A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpatialViz-Bench and provide readable main text, tables, figures, generation algorithms and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original model evaluations, an eight-participant human baseline, CoT comparisons and annotated error analyses, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v5 retains original evaluations and adds text-only, prompting, extraction and answer-format results, plus statistical and annotator-agreement analyses.

M1.justification: The four-ability benchmark framework, Python/FreeCAD generation pipeline and Algorithms 1–21 remain substantively unchanged. Expanded construction explanations do not establish a change to the underlying generation procedures.

E1.justification: The same 12 tasks and 1,180 benchmark problems remain. v5 adds evaluation without visual input and explicitly tests option-free Cube Counting in Table 6, extending input and answer requirements within existing tasks. Text/numeric-answer formats were already mentioned in v4.

E2.justification: v5 Table 2 adds Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as a text-only comparator. Matched appendix tables remove LLaVA-OneVision 7B/72B and InternVL2.5 8B/78B; rotation, folding and animation comparisons also remove InternVL2.5-38B. InternVL2.5-78B nevertheless appears in v5's new CoT significance Table 3. The main 27-MLLM comparison is retained.

E3.justification: v5 adds alternative CoT-prompt and extraction-rule conditions, explicit fill-in-the-blank scoring and a 100-case independent annotation check. The primary zero-shot setting, accuracy measure and human-evaluation protocol remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun using the expanded extractor.

E4.justification: Beyond v4's CoT ablation and error analyses, v5 tests dependence on visual input, sensitivity to prompt wording and extraction rules, and the assistance provided by answer options. Figure 4 also adds model- and task-level difficulty-sensitivity analyses. These substantially expand validation of the benchmark and its diagnostic findings.

E5.justification: v5 newly reports 95% Wilson confidence intervals, CoT p-values, significance-based difficulty comparisons and Cohen's kappa from 100 independently annotated errors, including per-category agreement in Table 5. v4 lacks these estimates. Neither version establishes repeated-run or seed-based uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Shared main-table model scores remain unchanged, but v5 adds substantial diagnostic results: text-only accuracy of 25.86%, prompt/extraction outcomes, difficulty-sensitivity findings and annotation agreement. Table 6 reports Cube Counting drops of 32.50 percentage points for GPT-4o and 14.17 for Gemini-2.5-pro when removing options. Several appendix model-result rows are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical calculations and generation algorithms in Appendix B are retained. The cognitive framework is condensed without substantively changing its definitions; no new theorem, formal assumption, derivation or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution lists and conclusions retain the same central claims: a cognitively grounded, scalable spatial-visualization benchmark, strong discrimination, substantial human–model gaps and predominantly visuospatial failure modes. The diagnostic title and additional validation do not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v5 adds performance-floor explanations for weak difficulty gradients, interprets answer options as clues or error-correction opportunities, and argues that parsing does not explain CoT degradation. It removes v4 Appendix F's discussion of manual cube-stack review, limited training-scale data and future tool-assisted evaluation. The central perception/transformation interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds the exact alternative prompt, detailed extraction regexes, direct string-matching instructions and fuller explanations of non-CoT model exclusions. Code/data links and retained hardware/model-version disclosures are unchanged. The manual cube-stack review disclosure is removed, without establishing that the underlying curation procedure changed.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to LEGO-Puzzles, Yin et al.'s spatial mental modeling, Shepard–Metzler, the Qwen2.5 technical report and MME-CoT. It acknowledges additional programmatic and mental-modeling benchmarks and reassigns contamination and narrow-coverage criticisms between Xu et al. and SRBench. The broad research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially condensed and reorganized: Spatial Visualization becomes a benchmark subsection, Dataset Characteristic moves to Appendix C, related work is compressed, and evaluation paragraphs receive extensive rewrites and descriptive headings. The evaluation appendices are reorganized, and the title and correspondence text change.

P2.justification: v5 adds the three-panel statistical Figure 4 and Tables 3–6, revises Figure 1, arranges error-distribution charts horizontally and reflows the main case-study illustration. Existing tables move or shrink as rows are removed. Appendix examples and detailed case-study images are retained under revised numbering.

improvement.justification: The new visual-dependence, robustness and answer-format controls strengthen validation of the unchanged benchmark, while agreement reporting helps assess its error taxonomy. The gain is limited by inconsistent kappa values—0.85 in Section 4.3.1 versus 0.8847 in Appendix E.6.3—extraction-drop entries in Table 4(b) that conflict with Table 2, and removal of the manual-review and dataset-scale caveat.
